limitations: This source ratchet recognizes named button/el/literalText/createElement constructors, static HTML tags and inline JavaScript. It is not an exhaustive JavaScript renderer analysis.
Dynamic labels/tags, embedded markup, semantic roles, duplicate declarations and external script dependencies remain explicit detection gaps, never inferred coverage.
Property-assigned labels, arbitrary wrappers, imported modules outside the listed source surface, CSS interactions and runtime-only branches require additional source review and behavioral scenarios.
Mappings qualify only their named assertion scenario. The remaining state gaps on each mapping are unresolved; no control or whole-site completeness is claimed.
Scenario title and ordered assertion tokens are static integrity anchors, not proof the test passed. CI must execute the actual associated test runner.
New or changed declarations fail without manifest registration. The explicit gap list and budget are reviewed configuration, not an immutable promise that gaps can never increase.
A declaration may link several reviewed state scenarios. None of these links removes the explicit remaining state gaps or qualifies an unresolved constructor.

Parameterized scenario recognition is limited to direct top-level expression statements calling it.each/test.each with a nonempty static finite numeric literal table; nested/function/short-circuit/conditional/skipped/runtime tables remain unknown. Anchors are source integrity only, and every linked scenario still needs actual runner evidence.

Filesystem discovery inventories every supported JS/HTML source under src/web/public, including nested files and the owned gesture bundle, and every owned TypeScript source under packages/xterm-zerolag-input/src. It needs no Git metadata and runs against the flattened Nix web root.

Only exact reviewed third-party distributions and the two compiled duplicate xterm outputs are excluded. Their entire owned TypeScript source tree is included; unknown vendor/generated neighbors and missing primary sources fail the scope ratchet. No additional behavior is inferred from these inputs.

Newly discovered declarations remain explicit gaps. Existing36 behavioral mappings, their scenario assertions and remaining state limits are preserved; broader source presence is not whole-site behavioral coverage.

The three exact owned generator scripts are also parsed as authored input for their appended browser alias constructors; those outputs are not described as third-party. Source discovery does not execute those scripts or qualify their bundle behavior.
Supported script formats are JS/MJS/CJS/JSX and TS/MTS/CTS/TSX; HTM and HTML use the HTML scanner. JSX/TSX markup is retained only as unresolved detection gaps, never inferred behavioral mappings.
